title: "Interactive network graphs in JavaScript with CanvasXpress"
description: "Build a draggable, force-directed network in the browser from nodes and edges — interactive and reproducible from one portable spec."
author: "Isaac Neuhaus"
date: "2026-10-31"
categories: [JavaScript, CanvasXpress, network, visualization]
image: "thumbnail.png"
---

A network graph shows **relationships**: nodes connected by edges, laid out so connected things sit
near each other. In the browser the common answer is to hand-roll a force simulation in D3 — a few
hundred lines. CanvasXpress is a JavaScript library at heart, so the whole thing is a `data` object
of nodes and edges plus a `config`.

## Load the library

```html
<link href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/neuhausi/canvasXpress@73.3.0/inst/htmlwidgets/lib/canvasXpress/canvasXpress.css" rel="stylesheet">
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/neuhausi/canvasXpress@73.3.0/inst/htmlwidgets/lib/canvasXpress/canvasXpress.min.js"></script>
```

## The markup and the spec

Nodes carry `id`, `name`, `group`; edges carry `id1`, `id2`, `value`. `colorNodeBy` colours by
community and `networkLayoutType: "forceDirected"` runs the physics.

```html
<canvas id="network" width="650" height="500"></canvas>
<script>
  var groups = ["Alpha", "Beta", "Gamma"], nodes = [], byGroup = {}, k = 0;
  groups.forEach(function (g) {
    byGroup[g] = [];
    for (var i = 0; i < 7; i++) {
      var nid = "n" + k; nodes.push({ id: nid, name: g + (i + 1), group: g });
      byGroup[g].push(nid); k++;
    }
  });

  var edges = [];
  groups.forEach(function (g) {                         // dense within a community
    var m = byGroup[g];
    for (var i = 0; i < m.length; i++)
      for (var j = i + 1; j < m.length; j++)
        if (Math.random() < 0.5)
          edges.push({ id1: m[i], id2: m[j], value: 1 + Math.floor(Math.random() * 5) });
  });
  for (var e = 0; e < 6; e++) {                         // a few cross-community links
    var pair = groups.slice().sort(function () { return Math.random() - 0.5; }).slice(0, 2);
    var a = byGroup[pair[0]], b = byGroup[pair[1]];
    edges.push({ id1: a[Math.floor(Math.random() * a.length)],
                 id2: b[Math.floor(Math.random() * b.length)], value: 1 });
  }

  var config = {
    graphType: "Network",
    networkLayoutType: "forceDirected",
    colorNodeBy: "group",
    nodeSize: 25,
    showAnimation: true,
    title: "A small community network"
  };

  new CanvasXpress("network", { nodes: nodes, edges: edges }, config);
</script>
```

## Live result

```{=html}
<link href="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/neuhausi/canvasXpress@73.3.0/inst/htmlwidgets/lib/canvasXpress/canvasXpress.css" rel="stylesheet">
<script src="https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/gh/neuhausi/canvasXpress@73.3.0/inst/htmlwidgets/lib/canvasXpress/canvasXpress.min.js"></script>
<canvas id="networkLive" width="650" height="500"></canvas>
<script>
(function () {
  function draw() {
    if (typeof CanvasXpress === "undefined") { return setTimeout(draw, 60); }
    var groups = ["Alpha", "Beta", "Gamma"], nodes = [], byGroup = {}, k = 0;
    groups.forEach(function (g) {
      byGroup[g] = [];
      for (var i = 0; i < 7; i++) {
        var nid = "n" + k; nodes.push({ id: nid, name: g + (i + 1), group: g });
        byGroup[g].push(nid); k++;
      }
    });
    var edges = [];
    groups.forEach(function (g) {
      var m = byGroup[g];
      for (var i = 0; i < m.length; i++)
        for (var j = i + 1; j < m.length; j++)
          if (Math.random() < 0.5)
            edges.push({ id1: m[i], id2: m[j], value: 1 + Math.floor(Math.random() * 5) });
    });
    for (var e = 0; e < 6; e++) {
      var pair = groups.slice().sort(function () { return Math.random() - 0.5; }).slice(0, 2);
      var a = byGroup[pair[0]], b = byGroup[pair[1]];
      edges.push({ id1: a[Math.floor(Math.random() * a.length)],
                   id2: b[Math.floor(Math.random() * b.length)], value: 1 });
    }
    new CanvasXpress("networkLive", { nodes: nodes, edges: edges },
      { graphType: "Network", networkLayoutType: "forceDirected", colorNodeBy: "group",
        nodeSize: 25, showAnimation: true, title: "A small community network" });
  }
  draw();
})();
</script>
```

Drag any node and the layout settles around it; hover to read the label. The three communities
separate on their own because within-group edges outnumber the cross-group ones.

## Why "reproducible"

The nodes, edges and `config` **are** the figure — one portable JSON spec that renders the same from
R, Python, or a web page.
